Yuchang Gil 길유창

M.S.–Ph.D. Student · Dept. of Smart Air Mobility, Korea Aerospace University

I investigate detonation propulsion and supercritical regenerative cooling through experiments and numerical simulations. I designed and built a pre-detonator test rig for rotating detonation engines (RDEs) to characterize flame acceleration and deflagration-to-detonation transition (DDT); the resulting first-author paper in Fire (2025) was selected as the issue cover article.

On the numerical side, I study supercritical heat transfer of hydrocarbon mixtures in regenerative cooling channels using ANSYS Fluent and develop multi-objective genetic-algorithm surrogate fuels (POSF-10325, JP-8, RP-3), published as co-first-author papers in Fuel (2026) and Applied Thermal Engineering (2026). I began my propulsion work by designing, building and launching a hybrid rocket in the Korea Aerospace University rocket club (S.R.S.), and later contributed as a co-author to the Polaris-1 small liquid rocket.

Research Areas & Methods

Detonation Propulsion Experiments

Design, construction and operation of a pre-detonator test rig, plus micro pulse detonation engine/combustor (Micro PDE/PDC) experiments. High-speed schlieren and chemiluminescence imaging combined with dynamic pressure measurements to resolve shock–flame interactions and DDT.

Supercritical Regenerative Cooling CFD

ANSYS Fluent simulations of supercritical hydrocarbon flows in regenerative cooling channels for hypersonic (scramjet) propulsion, analyzing heat-transfer deterioration (HTD), buoyancy-induced secondary flows, and thermophysical property variations near the pseudo-critical point.

Surrogate Fuel Optimization

Multi-objective genetic-algorithm design of 4-component surrogates that match the thermophysical properties and distillation curves of real aviation fuels (JP-8, RP-3, POSF-10325), with ignition behavior checked by CHEMKIN kinetic modeling.

Selected Publications

First- and co-first-author SCI journal articles.

Fire 2025 · First Author (Cover Article)

Impact of a Variable Blockage Ratio on the Detonation Transition in a Pre-Detonator

Compared converging, constant, and diverging obstacle layouts sharing a mean blockage ratio of 0.5 across equivalence ratios of 0.64–1.6, demonstrating that the converging layout promotes the earliest and most reliable detonation onset.

Details →
Fuel 2026 · Co-First Author

Development of Jet Surrogate Fuel Formulated by Genetic Algorithm

Simultaneously optimized species selection (4 of 16 candidates) and mole fractions to formulate surrogates for POSF-10325, JP-8, and RP-3, achieving target property errors within ±1 % and validating against ignition delay and reactor experiments.

Details →
Applied Thermal Engineering 2026 · Co-First Author

Distinct Roles of Critical Pressure and Temperature in Supercritical Heat Transfer of Binary Hydrocarbon Mixtures

Separated the effects of critical pressure and temperature during supercritical heat-transfer deterioration (HTD), showing that the operating-to-critical pressure gap governs deterioration severity while the pseudo-critical temperature determines its onset location.
